title: Patients', family members' and healthcare professionals' attitudes towards medical assistance in dying on psychiatric grounds: systematic review of qualitative literature.
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Medical assistance in dying on psychiatric grounds (MAiD-PS) is a complex issue of emerging international importance. Beyond existing research on the moral and legal aspects of MAiD-PS, more studies are now examining the attitudes of those directly involved. However, systematic comparison between the perspectives of patients, family members and healthcare professionals is still lacking. This paper provides an overview of attitudes towards MAiD-PS across different countries, with specific attention paid to contrasting perspectives between respondent groups. This preregistered systematic review and metasynthesis of qualitative studies followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses and Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research guidelines. Six databases were searched for 'attitudes', 'medical assistance in dying' and 'psychiatry'. Qualitative studies on attitudes towards MAiD-PS were included. Conceptual and normative papers were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Thematic analysis was employed to conduct the metasynthesis. Twelve qualitative studies (2018-2024) were included. Studies were categorised by population: patients, family members and healthcare professionals. Metasynthesis resulted in 15 themes. Despite substantial thematic overlap between groups, results show conceptual differences in their interpretations. Patients and family members primarily prioritise individual self-determination and dignity, whereas healthcare professionals focus on relational autonomy and the clinical challenges of establishing irremediability. This is the first review to systematically compare perspectives across stakeholder groups, showing that attitudes towards MAiD-PS are intertwined with the respondent's role. The identified contrasts underscore the need for open discussions in which all stakeholder perspectives are recognised and heard, eventually leading to clinical guidelines that take into account stakeholder perspectives.

title: The Transition of Feeding and Swallowing Difficulties From Birth to Adult Age in 23 Cri du Chat Syndrome Patients.
journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
abstract: Cri du chat syndrome (CdCs) is a rare genetic disorder caused by deletions of various sizes in the short arm of chromosome 5. The clinical course of CdCs involves neurodevelopmental and communication features, including feeding and swallowing difficulties. Dysphagia is common in CdCs, with reported deficits meeting criteria for pediatric feeding and swallowing disorder, yet characteristics and symptom progression from birth to adulthood have not been studied in depth. The aim of this article is to describe the prevalence and evolution of feeding and swallowing difficulties from birth to adult age. Adult patients with a confirmed cytogenetic and/or molecular diagnosis of CdCs were recruited from the Italian Cri du chat Association (ABC Associazione Bambini Cri du chat Onlus, Italy) over a 1-year period. Pathogenic variants, along with key information regarding oral-motor features, were collected. Twenty-three patients were included in this study (10 M; mean age 34.3 years; SD 8.3 years; median age 34 years; age range 18-50 years). None of them were siblings to other participants. All patients were of Italian origin. While the whole cohort underwent typical karyotyping, Array CGH was performed in 13 patients. In individuals with CdCs, feeding and swallowing difficulties begin in the neonatal period (96%) and persist throughout life. Adulthood is characterized by a marked dependence on carers and has a significant impact on the family's care burden. In the present study, we reported their prevalence and evolution from birth to adulthood. Our study may improve the patients' management and support the introduction of preventive supporting habits in this rare disease.

title: Barriers and enablers to the implementation of dementia biomarkers into specialist clinical practice: A scoping review.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Dementia biomarkers are rapidly transitioning to routine clinical care, yet guidance on their real-world implementation within specialist settings remains limited. While implementation barriers and enablers are increasingly catalogued in the literature, how these factors systematically map across health systems, and where implementation evidence is critically missing, remains poorly defined. Identifying the barriers, enablers, and strategies that influence implementation is crucial to achieving timely and accessible dementia diagnosis. To address this gap, we conducted a scoping review using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to map the barriers, enablers, and strategies associated with implementing dementia biomarkers in routine specialist clinical practice. Searching MEDLINE, Embase, and Emcare, we screened 3744 articles and included 30 (11 primary studies, 14 reviews, 3 perspectives, 2 policy papers). Using the CFIR's structured domains revealed that while literature extensively addresses biomarker validity, access, and acceptability, specific operational processes for integrating biomarkers into secondary and tertiary clinical workflows remain sparse. Existing evidence supports adoption in principle but lacks framework-guided, empirical implementation pathways. By applying explicit CFIR structuring, this review demonstrates that the field remains concentrated at conceptual readiness, highlighting an urgent need to transition from barrier identification to empirical implementation studies evaluating real-world implementation across varied specialist care settings.

title: Multidimensional educational social determinants are associated with social cognition in healthy aging across Latin America.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Educational inequality is significantly associated with cognitive aging in Latin America, yet its association with social cognition, a clinically relevant domain in brain aging and dementia, remains poorly understood. We introduce educational social determinants (ESD), a multidimensional framework capturing familial, institutional, and individual educational contexts, to examine its association with social cognition beyond traditional years of schooling. We analyzed 1327 cognitively unimpaired adults from the Multi-Partner Consortium to Expand Dementia Research in Latin America (ReDLat) consortium across six countries. We specified two hierarchical SEM frameworks. First, ESD was modeled as a second-order latent construct integrating home environment, personal education, and institutional context. Second, an integrated structural model tested the joint associations of ESD and a life-course social exposome (deprivation, conflict, violence, and social network) with social cognition. The initial ESD model showed excellent fit (Comparative Fit Index [CFI] = 0.967) and explained 38% of the variance in social cognition, significantly outperforming years of education alone (R2 = 0.381 vs. 0.279; z = -2.63, p = 0.009). Institutional context showed the strongest loading (β = 0.93), highlighting the contribution of structural educational inequalities to the ESD construct. In the integrated model (R2 = 0.43), where both latent constructs were modeled simultaneously, ESD showed the strongest association with social cognition (β = 0.67, p < 0.001). The social exposome was also independently associated with social cognition (β = -0.26, p = 0.001), primarily driven by material deprivation and emotional support. ESD was strongly associated with the social exposome (β = 0.68), indicating a close relationship between educational conditions and broader social exposures. ESD provides a robust framework for capturing structural educational inequalities that traditional metrics overlook. The observed associations of institutional and familial educational contexts with social cognition support the relevance of educational equity as a potentially modifiable factor associated with cognitive resilience in diverse aging populations.

title: Metabolomics in the First Hour After Experimental Rotational Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: To understand the pathophysiology of traumatic brain injury (TBI), it is important to characterize the earliest events of injury, which provide the foundation for subsequent biochemical, structural, and functional changes. Fifty-six Sprague-Dawley rats were used in a standardized model for rotational acceleration-induced TBI to investigate early metabolic patterns. The animals were divided into four groups euthanized at 0, 10, 20, and 60 min ± 30 s postinjury with 7 experimental trauma and sham-operated rats in each group. Brain homogenates were analyzed using a targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) panel encompassing approximately 1,500 analytes. Samples from the anterior corpus callosum, where the model shows the most abundant injuries were chosen for analysis from the 0, 10, and 60 min trauma and sham groups. Homogenates from the 0 min and 60 min survival groups were also collected from lateral white matter, where the model shows the least injuries. Glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light (Nf-L) were analyzed with NULISA in experimental trauma and sham-operated rats in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the 0, 20, and 60 min groups. Plasma GFAP showed a significant increase in trauma rats with survival times of 60 min compared with 60 min sham rats and a transient increase of Nf-L was seen in the 0 min trauma group compared with sham, but no other significant changes were seen of these brain injury markers in plasma or CSF. The metabolomic pattern was then compared between groups. In trauma rats, triacylglycerols showed an immediate increase in concentration in the corpus callosum in the 0 min experimental trauma group compared to the lateral white matter in experimental trauma groups and all sham-operated groups but decreased in concentration to the levels of the lateral white matter and sham-operated groups after 10 and 60 min. The membrane-associated lipid class phosphatidylethanolamines (PE) were reduced in all trauma groups compared with sham-operated animals. In anterior corpus callosum, lysophosphatidylcholine 18:2 (LPC 18:2) showed a significant increase and glucosylceramides showed a significant decrease in concentration in all experimental trauma groups compared with sham-operated groups. Since LPC can initiate inflammation and glucosylceramide microdomains are critical for axonal excitability and synaptic transmission, the results can contribute to our understanding of the sequence of molecular events in the early phase of TBI. The results offer a trauma-related biopattern and may serve as a foundation for further studies to find early diagnostic biomarkers, some of which may be drug targets for urgent intervention therapy in rotational TBI. In the postmortem setting, specific analysis of these molecules in anterior corpus callosum might prove feasible for detection of rotational TBI, particular in cases where no, or only few microscopic bleedings are seen.

title: Reduced spike adaptation in RHEB/mTORC1-hyperactive excitatory neurons influences network hyperactivity.
abstract: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway plays a crucial role in structural brain development by regulating cell growth, metabolism and other cellular processes. Hyperactivation of this pathway causes refractory epilepsy and enhanced network activity through increased synaptic connectivity. However, patch-clamp recordings of neurons in which the mTOR pathway is hyperactive revealed reduced intrinsic excitability. To unravel the mechanism underlying this paradoxical finding, we combine whole-cell recordings from dissociated murine hippocampal neurons overexpressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation, with an in silico model to connect cellular changes to network dynamics. We found an increased rheobase, decreased depolarization-induced excitability and increased afterhyperpolarization current in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, confirming hypo-excitability. Further characterization of spike-trains revealed a lack of adaptation in these neurons, enabling neurons to reach shorter interspike intervals in response to higher current injections. We built a computational model of the neurons that reproduces the electrophysiological parameters we measured. This model revealed the interaction between the afterhyperpolarization current and voltage-dependent refractory mechanisms as a potential cause for the reduction in spike adaptation. Network simulation revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization current, and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity, suggesting the altered passive properties in RHEB-p.P37L neurons as a cause of reduced burst rhythmicity on network level. Our findings indicate that, in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, excitability is regulated in a state-dependent manner, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with poor adaptation, promoting high-frequency firing in high-input states. Based on our results, we propose that, in addition to altered synaptic connectivity, differences in state-dependent neuronal excitability underlie mTOR-hyperactivity-induced disruptions of network activity. KEY POINTS: The mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) pathway is essential for brain development, and hyperactivation of the pathway causes refractory epilepsy and increased neuronal network activity. Neurons with induced mTORC1-hyperactivity display intrinsic hypo-excitability at the single-cell level but exhibit stronger synaptic connectivity in networks than controls. Single-cell recordings from murine primary hippocampal neurons expressing the gain-of-function Ras-homolog enriched in brain (RHEB)-p.P37L mutation reveal increased afterhyperpolarization currents and a marked reduction in spike-frequency adaptation, allowing neurons to fire at shorter interspike intervals during strong current injection. A biophysically constrained computational neuron model recapitulating the biological single-cell intrinsic properties reproduced faster firing in response to strong current injection, and revealed how passive properties, afterhyperpolarization and synaptic connectivity contribute to aberrant network activity. The findings demonstrate state-dependent regulation of excitability in mTORC1-hyperactive neurons, where baseline hypo-excitability coexists with impaired adaptation and high-frequency firing, suggesting that altered intrinsic excitability, in addition to increased synaptic connectivity, contributes to mTOR-driven network dysfunction.

title: Pain Interference and Buprenorphine Dosing in Patients With Opioid Use Disorder and Chronic Pain: A Secondary Analysis From the Prescription Opioid Addiction Treatment Study.
abstract: Chronic pain is a significant comorbid condition among patients with opioid use disorder (OUD), yet little is known about the relationship between pain intensity and interference, and prescribed buprenorphine (BUP) dose. The current study examined the association between pain intensity, interference, and concurrent pain medication use with BUP doses, and differences in pain outcomes between baseline and 12 weeks of BUP treatment. This study of individuals with OUD and chronic pain (n = 111) is a secondary analysis of data collected in a National Institute on Drug Abuse Clinical Trials Network study. Logistic regression models were used to investigate the association between pain intensity and interference and BUP doses. Participants reported significant improvement in pain intensity and interference from baseline to 12 weeks of BUP treatment. In the adjusted analysis, greater pain interference with mood (adjusted odds ratio [﻿aOR] = 1.55, 95% confidence interval [CI 1.03-2.32], P = .036) and enjoyment of life (aOR = 1.54, 95% CI [1.03-2.29], P = .033) were significantly associated with higher odds of receiving higher BUP doses. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (34.5%, n = 204), acetaminophen and/or aspirin (31.3%, n = 185), and opioid analgesics (25.7%, n = 152) were most frequently used by participants to treat pain. Concurrent pain medication use was not significantly associated with odds of receiving higher BUP doses (aOR = 0.79, 95% CI [0.38-1.66], P = .533). Among individuals with OUD and chronic pain, greater pain interference with mood and enjoyment of life were associated with receiving higher BUP doses.

title: Effects of Ganaxolone on Anxiety-Like Behaviors in Single Prolonged Stress-Exposed Mice.
abstract: Current post-traumatic stress disorder treatments, primarily selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, show suboptimal efficacy. Ganaxolone, a synthetic neurosteroid and positive allosteric modulator of GABAA receptors, may offer a novel therapeutic approach by enhancing both synaptic and extrasynaptic GABAergic inhibition. This study investigated the effects of ganaxolone on anxiety-like behaviors and late post-stress corticolimbic allopregnanolone and corticosterone levels in a mouse model of single prolonged stress. Male BALB/c mice underwent single prolonged stress. After a 14-day incubation period, ganaxolone (3.75, 7.5, or 15 mg/kg, i.p.) or vehicle was administered daily for five consecutive days (Days 15-19). The rotarod, open field, elevated plus maze, forced swim, and social interaction tests were performed. Allopregnanolone and corticosterone levels in the prefrontal cortex and amygdala were assessed using ELISA. Single prolonged stress induced a distinct anxiety-like phenotype in open field and elevated plus maze tests. Ganaxolone treatment significantly attenuated anxiety-like behaviors. Ganaxolone at 7.5 mg/kg significantly increased open field center time, while all three ganaxolone doses significantly increased elevated plus maze open-arm time. No statistically significant differences were observed in locomotor activity, social interaction, forced swim test immobility, or corticolimbic allopregnanolone and corticosterone levels. Ganaxolone showed anxiolytic-like effects in single prolonged stress-exposed mice, particularly in the elevated plus maze. These findings suggest that ganaxolone may be further investigated as a potential non-benzodiazepine treatment approach for anxiety-dominant symptoms in post-traumatic stress disorder.

title: Renal resistive index and serum creatinine changes in icu patients receiving vasopressor therapy: a prospective cohort study.
journal: Journal of health, population, and nutrition
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common complication in critically ill patients receiving vasopressor therapy. Serum creatinine, the standard biomarker for AKI, rises relatively late and is influenced by several non-renal factors. The renal resistive index (RRI), measured by Doppler ultrasonography, may provide an earlier assessment of intrarenal hemodynamic changes. This study evaluated the association between serial RRI measurements and renal function in vasopressor-treated intensive care unit (ICU) patients. In this prospective single-center cohort study, 120 adult ICU patients requiring norepinephrine infusion were enrolled. RRI, serum creatinine, urine output, mean arterial pressure, and norepinephrine dose were recorded daily for seven days or until ICU discharge or death. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Multivariable regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses were used to assess the association and discriminatory performance of baseline RRI for AKI occurrence during the seven-day observation period. AKI developed in 38 patients (31.7%). Patients with AKI had significantly higher baseline RRI than those without AKI (0.79 ± 0.07 vs. 0.68 ± 0.06, P < 0.001). RRI remained persistently elevated in the AKI group, whereas it gradually declined in patients without AKI (all P < 0.05). Baseline RRI was independently associated with higher Day-7 serum creatinine (β = 0.28, P = 0.014) and AKI development (OR = 2.15, 95% CI 1.12-4.14, P = 0.021). Baseline RRI showed moderate discrimination for AKI (AUC = 0.71, 95% CI 0.62-0.80). Patients with elevated baseline RRI had longer ICU and hospital stays. Elevated baseline and persistently increased RRI were independently associated with subsequent AKI and worsening renal function in vasopressor-treated ICU patients. Serial bedside RRI assessment may complement conventional biomarkers for early identification of patients at increased risk of AKI.

title: Cell type- and tau lesion-specific accumulation of phospho-Ser65 ubiquitin in primary tauopathies.
abstract: Defective mitochondrial quality control is increasingly implicated in tau-mediated neurodegeneration, but how distinct tau lesions in different cell types interact with PINK1-PRKN-mediated mitophagy remains unclear. Phosphorylated ubiquitin at serine 65 (pS65-Ub) is the joint product of PINK1-PRKN signaling. Significant deposition of pS65-Ub has been previously demonstrated in autopsy brains from patients with Lewy body disease, Alzheimer disease, and MAPT mutation-associated frontotemporal lobar degeneration, where increased pS65-Ub signal was particularly strongly associated with early neuronal tau pathology. We here expanded the analyses to 92 postmortem human brains comparing neuropathologically normal controls and cases of primary age-related tauopathy (PART), Pick's disease (PiD), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and corticobasal degeneration (CBD). Using pS65-Ub and pS202-tau immunohistochemistry in selectively vulnerable regions, deep learning-based quantification of tau lesion subtypes, and single-cell co-localization analyses, we found considerable disease-, cell type-, and tau inclusion-specific differences in pS202-tau and pS65-Ub accumulation. Although pS202-tau burden was elevated across all primary tauopathies in their respective vulnerable regions, the extent of pathology and predominant tau inclusion types varied markedly among diseases. pS65-Ub positive cells were most abundant in the hippocampus of PART and PiD but were sparse in the primary motor cortex of PSP and especially in CBD, despite extensive tau pathology. In both PART and PiD, pS65-Ub primarily accumulated in neurons containing tau inclusions, with significantly greater intracellular burden and more frequent large vacuolar structures in PART. The density of pS65-Ub/tau double-positive cells strongly correlated with tau tangle burden in PART but not with Pick body burden in PiD. Together, our findings revealed marked heterogeneity in the distribution, density, intracellular abundance, and morphology of pS65-Ub deposits across affected brain regions in primary tauopathies, highlighting pS65-Ub as a potential marker for differential diagnosis of neuronal tau-associated disorders in tauopathies.

title: Cannabis use among psychiatric in-patients: Prevalence, clinical characteristics and hospital outcomes.
abstract: Cannabis use is common among people receiving psychiatric care and may be associated with more complex clinical presentations and inpatient trajectories, but its prevalence and association with hospitalization outcomes remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of documented cannabis use during psychiatric hospitalizations and to explore associated socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics. Retrospective observational study analyzing routinely collected data from the electronic health records of patients admitted between 2019 and 2024. Descriptive statistics and multivariable analyses were conducted to examine associations of cannabis use with length of stay, seclusion and restraint. Psychiatric inpatient units of the Groupe Hospitalier Universitaire (GHU) Paris Psychiatrie et Neurosciences hospital group, a network of public psychiatric hospitals in Paris, France. 32 429 hospital stays corresponding to 17 040 individual adult patients. The median age was 40 years (interquartile range 28-54) and 45.4% were female. Documented cannabis use was the main exposure, identified through multiple complementary sources: a positive urine toxicology result, presence of a cannabis-related diagnosis in structured clinical data and a natural language processing keyword search algorithm applied to free clinical notes. Outcomes were length of stay, seclusion and restraint. Covariates included socio-demographic, clinical and hospitalization characteristics such as age, sex, diagnostic category, comorbidities, housing status and legal admission status. Cannabis use was documented in 25.0% of patients, and an overall increase was observed over the study period despite year-to-year fluctuations. Compared with individuals without documented use, those with identified use were more often male, younger and had higher rates of psychotic disorders and comorbidity. In multivariable models, the association between documented cannabis use and length of stay varied according to legal admission status, whereas no interaction with legal admission status was observed for seclusion or restraint. Cannabis use was associated with longer length of stay, with adjusted ratios of mean length of stay of 1.22 [95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.16-1.27] for voluntary admissions, 1.23 (95% CI = 1.17-1.29) for involuntary admissions under a civil procedure, 1.39 (95% CI = 1.28-1.50) for state-ordered admissions and 1.64 (95% CI = 1.24-2.16) for incarcerated and forensic patients. Documented cannabis use was also associated with higher odds of seclusion [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.73, 95% CI = 1.56-1.91] and restraint (aOR = 1.88, 95% CI = 1.48-2.37). Cannabis use appears to occur in about a quarter of psychiatric inpatients in Paris, France, and prevalence is rising; it appears to be associated with longer (vs. shorter) hospitalizations and higher odds of coercive interventions (vs. no coercive interventions) during the stay.

title: Effect of APOE and LPA genotypes on the risk of dementia after myocardial infarction: a clinic-based cohort study.
abstract: Survivors of myocardial infarction (MI) face elevated risk of subsequent cognitive decline, yet the relative contributions of neurodegenerative susceptibility (APOE4) and lipid-mediated vascular burden (LPA risk variants) to post-MI dementia remain unclear, particularly in Asian populations historically underrepresented in dementia genetics research. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 4,788 patients with confirmed MI enrolled in the China Medical University Hospital precision medicine program (January 1, 2004-December 31, 2021), with directly genotyped APOE (rs429358, rs7412) and LPA (rs10455872, rs3798220) variants linked to longitudinal electronic health records and the Taiwan National Death Registry. Patients were classified into four genetic risk groups: low-risk, LPA-only, APOE4-only, and dual-risk. The primary outcome was incident all-cause dementia within a fixed 5-year follow-up and was analyzed using Cox proportional hazards regression. Sensitivity analyses included a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model to describe the cumulative incidence of dementia in the presence of death as a competing event, along with subgroup analyses by age, sex, and cardiovascular comorbidity. The median age was 61.2 years (IQR 51.9-70.3). Compared with the low-risk reference, APOE4 carriers had substantially elevated dementia risk (APOE4-only: HR 2.49, 95% CI 1.71-3.63; dual-risk: HR 2.63, 95% CI 1.32-5.26), whereas LPA-only carriers did not (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.73-1.95). Five-year dementia-free survival approached 96% in the low-risk and LPA-only groups, declined to approximately 93% in the APOE4-only group, and was lowest in dual-risk carriers. Kaplan-Meier curves showed accelerated divergence among APOE4 carriers at approximately 840 days post-MI. Associations were consistent across age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years; interaction p = 0.389) and sex (interaction p = 0.141) and remained robust in Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses. Among MI survivors in a real-world Asian genomic cohort, APOE4, but not LPA, was associated with subsequent dementia, suggesting a greater role for neurodegenerative susceptibility than Lp(a)-related lipid-vascular burden in post-MI cognitive outcomes. The apparent risk divergence around 840 days after MI remains exploratory and warrants further study.

title: Secretome and a novel dehydration-induced secretome of olfactory ensheathing cells promote neural stem cell viability and differentiation.
abstract: The olfactory ensheathing cell (OEC) secretome includes neurotrophic factors, cytokines, extracellular matrix proteins, and other signaling molecules that influence neuronal behavior including survival, proliferation, and differentiation. However, mechanisms by which the secretome modulates neuronal responses remain unclear. Here, we report a newly identified category of cell secretomes derived from human OECs, termed dehydration-induced secretome (DIS). This approach involves dehydrating OECs, followed by rehydration in phosphate-buffered saline, which induces the extensive formation of membrane vesicles ranging from exosome-sized particles to larger vesicles visible under a microscope. After centrifugation to remove larger vesicles, the supernatant containing both soluble proteins and exosome-sized vesicles was collected and defined as the DIS. We compared the DIS with our previously reported conventional secretome, analyzed protein expression patterns, and assessed functional implications. We also investigated the protective effects against oxidative stress, induction of quiescence, and differentiation promoting effect in neural stem cells (NSCs). Proteomic analysis revealed that both secretomes shared similar Gene Ontology terms, indicating functional overlap. Although more proteins were detected in the DIS, their abundance was generally lower than in the conventional secretome. However, the overall protein yield per cell was significantly higher in the DIS group. Only 36 proteins were shared between the two preparations and were primarily associated with actin filaments and glycolysis. Functionally, both the secretome and DIS promote NSC proliferation and differentiation with distinct molecular responses. DIS showed antioxidant activity primarily by reducing ROS accumulation in NSCs under H₂O₂-induced oxidative stress, which was associated with superoxide dismutase activity. Although both secretome and DIS stimulated NSC proliferation and differentiation, their effects on specific neuronal markers and pathways differed. Notably, DIS significantly promoted axonal branching and reduced the expression of quiescence markers more effectively than the conventional secretome. However, DIS did not enhance the expression of the ribosomal protein subunit 6, which was upregulated in the conventional secretome. Overall, DIS from OECs exhibited beneficial effects similar to those of the conventional secretome while offering a higher yield and reduced processing time. It also enabled potentially better responses of NSCs to oxidative stress and quiescence inhibition, making it a therapeutic candidate for neurological diseases. Not Applicable.

title: Korea10K integrates 10,239 whole genomes with multiomic and clinical health information as a Korean reference dataset.
abstract: Large-scale genome projects have advanced the characterization of human genetic diversity. However, the lack of deeply sequenced, multiomic resources representing the Korean population has limited systematic evaluation of population-specific variation and its functional and translational impact. We present Korea10K, a population-scale multiomic resource comprising 10,239 high-depth whole genomes (mean coverage 30 ×) with integrated molecular and phenotypic data. Analysis of 9,000 unrelated individuals enables near-complete discovery of ultra-rare variants (allele count > 2 and allele frequency ≤ 0.0005) and supports the construction of a high-resolution, population-specific imputation panel. Koreans exhibit pronounced autosomal genetic homogeneity together with a narrow Y-chromosomal and HLA-A allelic spectrum and comparatively deep mitochondrial lineage diversity, consistent with long-term demographic continuity. We further identify 16.4 million variants that alter CpG dinucleotide context, revealing widespread sequence-driven modulation of the genomic CG landscape. Notably, CG-eliminating variants generate loss of methylation signal and disrupt CpG probe targets in widely used methylation arrays, introducing a systematic source of bias in epigenome-wide association studies and epigenetic clock estimation. Korea10K establishes a high-resolution genomic and multiomic reference for the Korean population and reveals a previously unrecognized interaction between genetic variation and epigenomic measurement. This resource provides a foundation for precision medicine and highlights the need for ancestry-aware interpretation of molecular data.

title: Activation of alpha-2 adrenoceptors in locus coeruleus alleviates prenatal lipopolysaccharide-induced cognitive deficits in the offspring of rats.
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC), the brain's principal source of norepinephrine, critically regulates cognitive function. While our previous work established that prenatal lipopolysaccharide (LPS) exposure causes cognitive deficits in rat offspring, the underlying mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets remained unknown. In this study, we found that prenatal LPS exposure enhanced LC neuronal electrical activity and upregulated α2-adrenoceptors, tyrosine hydroxylase in the LC of 15-month-old rat offspring. Concurrently, both the LC and hippocampus exhibited Alzheimer's disease (AD)-like pathologies, including hyperphosphorylated tau, elevated Aβ42, and increased BACE1 and GSK3β expression in rat offspring. Notably, prenatal dexmedetomidine treatment, a highly selective α2-adrenoceptor agonist, significantly improved cognition and reversed these molecular and electrophysiological alterations. Direct microinjection of dexmedetomidine into the LC similarly suppressed hyperactive LC neurons. In conclusion, α-2 adrenoceptor receptors in LC plays an important role in cognitive deficits induced by prenatal LPS exposure, and Dexmedetomidine might be a promising agent in treating prenatal LPS-induced cognitive deficits in offspring rats.

title: Amygdala shows heterogeneous atrophy and tauopathy patterns across the AD continuum.
abstract: Amygdala shows early vulnerability in Alzheimer's disease (AD), although its substructures have been less studied than hippocampal subfields. Neuropathological evidence suggests that tau pathology affects amygdala subnuclei differentially, yet in vivo characterization of subregional amygdala atrophy, its relationship with tau burden, blood-based biomarkers, and cognitive outcomes across the AD continuum remains limited. Clarifying whether amygdala degeneration follows a homogeneous or regionally selective pattern, how it relates to plasma tau biomarkers, and whether it has functional consequences is essential for improving early detection and disease modeling. The study analyzed data from 197 participants, including 71 Aβ-negative cognitively normal individuals (Aβ- CN), 31 Aβ-positive cognitively normal individuals (Aβ+ CN), and 95 Aβ-positive cognitively impaired individuals (Aβ+ CI). All participants underwent T1-weighted MRI, [18F]-MK-6240 tau PET imaging, comprehensive neuropsychological assessment, and plasma pTau181 and pTau217 and Aβ42/40 analyses. Amygdala subregion volumes and tau standardized uptake value ratios (SUVr) were extracted using FreeSurfer-based segmentation and classified into basal, centro-medial, and lateral amygdala subregions. Regional amygdala volumes and SUVr were compared across groups and examined for associations with plasma tau biomarkers and cognitive performance. Mediation analyses assessed whether subregional amygdala atrophy mediated the relationship between tau pathology and cognition. Pronounced regional heterogeneity was observed within the amygdala. Atrophy of the centro-medial subregion was detectable at the preclinical stage of AD, preceding cognitive impairment. Lower centro-medial amygdala volume was significantly associated with higher plasma pTau181 and pTau217 levels, as well as with lower memory and executive scores. Mediation analyses demonstrated that amygdala tau-PET burden fully mediated the relationship between plasma pTau biomarkers and centro-medial amygdala volume, while centro-medial amygdala volume mediated the effect of tau pathology on memory performance. Although the centro-medial subregion showed the earliest and most pronounced atrophy, it did not exhibit a correspondingly higher local tau-PET burden than other amygdala subregions. These findings suggest that amygdala involvement in AD is regionally heterogeneous, appears early in the AD continuum, and has clinically significant cognitive consequences. Subregional quantification of the amygdala, particularly when combined with plasma pTau biomarkers, may provide sensitive early indicators of disease-related neurodegeneration, reflect network-level vulnerability, and improve understanding of cognitive decline, confirming its potential utility as a biomarker in AD research and clinical practice.

title: Hyperactive lateral hypothalamic GABAergic neurons drive abnormal aggression in neuroligin-3 R451C knock-in mice.
abstract: Aggressive behaviors represent a common and clinically challenging comorbidity in individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), yet the underlying neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the circuit-level pathology driving elevated aggression in Neuroligin-3 R451C knock-in mice (NL3R451C or KI mice). Aggressive behaviors in adult male mice were assessed using the resident-intruder and self-initiated aggression tests. Following the R-I test, c-Fos brain mapping was performed. Fiber photometry recording was used to capture neuronal activity in selected brain regions during attack bouts. Chemogenetic inhibition was applied to establish the causal role of specific neuronal subtypes or circuits in elevated aggression. Additive NL3 expression was used to examine the genetic contribution of distinct neuronal subpopulations to maladaptive aggression. NL3R451C mice exhibited heightened aggression and aggression-seeking behavior, accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in multiple brain regions, including the lateral hypothalamus (LH), prelimbic cortex (PrL), and ventral tegmental area (VTA). During attacks, KI mice showed enhanced calcium transients in LH GABAergic neurons and in PrL→LH glutamatergic neurons, but not in LH glutamatergic neurons. Critically, chemogenetic suppression of LH GABAergic neurons, or of LH neurons projecting to the VTA or periaqueductal gray (PAG), attenuated excessive aggression in KI mice, whereas inhibition of PrL→LH neurons had no effect. Moreover, additive NL3 expression specifically in LH GABAergic neurons, but not in PrL neurons, was sufficient to ameliorate the aggressive phenotype. First, the synaptic mechanisms underlying LH GABAergic dysregulation remain to be defined by direct electrophysiological characterization. Second, LH GABAergic neurons are heterogeneous, and our approach did not identify which specific subtype mediates excessive aggression. Third, our study used a male‑only design, reflecting the X‑linked clinical presentation of the NL3 R451C mutation. Future studies in female mutants could provide insights into sexual dimorphism and the underlying mechanisms. Fourth, NL3 rescue was achieved via viral‑mediated adult additive expression rather than developmental precisely genetic correcting. We conclude that hyperactive LH GABAergic neurons, caused by NL3 loss, is a core pathological mechanism underlying abnormal aggression in NL3R451C mouse model of ASD.

title: Hydrogen inhalation attenuates mechanical ventilation-induced postoperative cognitive dysfunction in aged mice by inhibiting the lung-brain axis-mediated transmission of pTau217-enriched extracellular vesicles.
abstract: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is an indispensable respiratory support strategy; however, increasing evidence suggests it may be a primary mediator of postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in vulnerable elderly patients. Despite this potential association, the precise lung-brain mechanisms through which MV-induced pulmonary stress mediates cognitive impairment and neurodegeneration remain unclear. To elucidate this interorgan cross-talk, we first conducted an observational analysis of plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) from elderly surgical patients. We identified an association of general anesthesia, surgery, and MV with a marked postoperative increase in circulating EV-derived pTau217 levels, accompanied by a proteomic signature enriched in lung-related markers. In an aged murine MV model, we mapped the rapid lung-to-brain trajectory of pTau217-enriched extracellular vesicles (0-6 h) and subsequent microglial activation and cognitive impairment. The results of integrated scRNA-seq and metabolomic profiling revealed that these EVs originated from bronchial epithelial cells, suggesting severe metabolic disturbance. The inhalation of hydrogen (H2) effectively averted this metabolic crisis, thereby inhibiting local Tau hyperphosphorylation and halting the release of pTau217-enriched EVs. This upstream blockade subsequently prevented microglial activation and rescued cognitive performance. These findings define a pathological lung-brain axis in which MV-induced metabolic disruption drives the EV-mediated spread of pTau217 to precipitate POCD in aged mice. Importantly, H2 therapy restores pulmonary metabolic homeostasis to halt this transmission at its source, suggesting a potential targeted intervention to preserve the aging brain in the perioperative period.

title: Childhood inductive reasoning, cardiovascular and cardiometabolic morbidity and dementia risk - a population representative cohort study across six decades.
abstract: Higher cognitive ability in late adolescence and young adulthood associate with reduced risk of dementia, but such assessments are influenced by educational selection. Whether specific cognitive abilities earlier in childhood associate with later dementia risk, independent of known associations with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes, remains unclear. We studied a Swedish population-representative birth cohort with cognitive testing at age 13 (n = 10,539 born in 1948). Dementia and somatic morbidity were ascertained from nationwide inpatient and cause-of-death registers through November 2025 (> 6 decades). Cox models estimated associations between childhood inductive reasoning, verbal and spatial ability scores and dementia, somatic morbidity, CVD and diabetes, each modelled as outcomes and as time-varying covariates in dementia models. During follow-up, 287 individuals (2.7%) developed dementia. Higher childhood inductive reasoning associated with lower risk of dementia (HR per SD = 0.84, 95% CI 0.72-0.98), somatic morbidity, CVD (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.83-0.92), and diabetes (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.79-0.91). Verbal and spatial abilities were not independently associated with dementia. Somatic morbidity, CVD, and diabetes associated with dementia risk (HRs ~ 1.75-2.13), but only modestly attenuated the inductive reasoning-dementia association (HRs ~ 0.84-0.85). Findings replicated in an expanded cohort including individuals born in 1953 (total n = 19,919) and were robust to adjustment for parental and midlife education. Higher childhood inductive reasoning was associated with lower dementia risk across six decades, and this relationship was not substantially attenuated by adjustment for education or clinically manifest cardiovascular or cardiometabolic disease. These findings are consistent with a life-course perspective in which early neurodevelopmental characteristics contribute to dementia risk alongside major vascular and metabolic risk factors.

title: Inflammasomes: central mediators of neuroinflammatory neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.
abstract: As life expectancy increases worldwide, the proportion of people aged 65 and older is expected to double by 2050 and these global demographic shifts will be accompanied by an increase in age-related neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). AD is the leading cause of dementia worldwide, characterized by progressive cognitive decline linked to amyloid beta accumulation, tau pathology, neuronal cell death and chronic neuroinflammation. PD is the most common movement disorder worldwide, characterized by progressive motor decline linked to alpha-synuclein accumulation, formation of Lewy bodies and neurites, dopaminergic neuron death, as well as chronic neuroinflammation. Increasing evidence implicates inflammasomes, intracellular multiprotein complexes that orchestrate innate immune responses, as key drivers of the neuroinflammatory milieu in AD and PD. The NLRP3 inflammasome, mostly expressed by microglia, has been shown to activate caspase-1, resulting in the cleavage and release of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 and promoting pyroptotic cell death within the central nervous system. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms of inflammasome activation, their pathological involvement in AD and PD, and the genetic underpinnings supporting their role. It further highlights emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at modulating inflammasome activity, evaluating preclinical outcomes and clinical trial progress. Understanding inflammasome dynamics provides critical insight into AD and PD pathophysiology and presents promising targets for future disease-modifying treatments.

title: Galectin-3 worsens microglia-mediated synaptic engulfment and neuroinflammatory responses after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Activated microglia-mediated aberrant synaptic phagocytosis is an important contributor to neurological deficits following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Galectin-3 (Gal-3), a pivotal regulator of microglial activity, is increased after TBI. However, its role in microglia-mediated synaptic phagocytosis and associated neuroinflammation remains unclear. Microglial phagocytic activity post-TBI was analyzed using public single-cell RNA sequencing datasets from GEO. The function of Gal-3 was investigated in a mouse model of controlled cortical impact by intraperitoneal administration of the selective inhibitor TD139. Sensorimotor and cognitive functions, microglial heterogeneity, synaptic engulfment, and neuroinflammation were assessed using behavioral tests, immunostaining, western blotting, and RT-qPCR. Gal-3 expression was specifically upregulated in phagocytic microglia following TBI. Pharmacological inhibition of Gal-3 by TD139 alleviated long-term sensorimotor and cognitive dysfunction and reduced cerebral tissue loss. Additionally, TD139 treatment promoted microglial heterogeneity, elevated the expression of anti-inflammatory factors, and inhibited excessive microglial synaptic engulfment, thereby attenuating synapse loss and preserving synaptic integrity. Microglial Gal-3 drives neuroinflammation and aberrant synaptic phagocytosis, contributing to neurological deficits following TBI. These findings identify Gal-3 as a promising therapeutic target for TBI intervention.

title: A peroxidase-mimetic platinum nanocluster induces concurrent DNA damage and oxidative cleavage in paediatric glioblastoma cells.
abstract: The impermeability of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), formed by a monolayer of endothelial cells, remains a major obstacle for delivering chemotherapeutic drugs to the brain. Ultra-small nanoparticles, particularly nanoclusters smaller than 2 nm, offer a promising strategy to overcome this challenge. Here, we investigate the anti-cancer efficacy and underlying mechanisms of two sizes of platinum-based nanoparticles; platinum nanoclusters (PtNCs: 2 nm) and platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs: 10 nm), synthesized using bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a stabilizer. In this study, PtNCs and PtNPs were tested against paediatric glioblastoma (p-GBM) cells, and were shown to induce cell death, prevent cell migration, and cause cell reproductive death. The mechanism of action of the PtNCs and PtNPs was investigated and compared with cisplatin by examining oxidative stress status, DNA damage, cell cycle arrest, and cell apoptosis. PtNCs exhibited promising catalytic ability under acidic conditions and physiological temperature. They showed the ability to generate free radicals to induce oxidative stress in p-GBM cells, thus causing DNA double strand breaks and G2/M phase cell cycle arrest. Conversely, PtNPs induced S phase cell cycle arrest by causing DNA crosslinking. These findings demonstrate that the cell death mechanism of Pt-based nanoparticles is critically size-dependent. This construct therefore has the potential for an improved anti-cancer treatment for paediatric glioblastoma with negligible cytotoxicity towards the normal organs. It is suggested that PtNCs could provide a promising treatment for p-GBM, and an alternative to conventional platinum-based drugs.

title: Small extracellular vesicles from pain-insensitive individuals modulate sensory-like neurons' responses in vitro.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles are emerging regulators of intercellular signalling in the nervous system, including mechanisms controlling sensory neuron excitability and pain processing. Marsili syndrome, a rare condition characterized by congenital pain insensitivity, provides a unique human model for investigating these pathways. Here, we show that urinary small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) derived from Marsili subjects reduce the responsiveness in differentiated sensory-like F-11 neurons. Marsili sEVs exhibited reduced size, comparable particle concentration, and a distinct microRNA cargo characterized by increased levels of miR-135a-5p and miR-138-5p and reduced miR-183 expression. Functionally, Marsili sEVs attenuated membrane depolarization and intracellular Ca²⁺ influx following inflammatory stimulation and KCl activation, indicating reduced responsiveness in differentiated F-11 cells. These effects were associated with marked downregulation of the potassium channel modulatory subunit KCNV1. Overall, our findings suggest that urinary sEVs from individuals with Marsili syndrome may contribute to the regulation of sensory neuron-like responsiveness by transferring bioactive molecular cargo. These findings identify urinary sEVs as candidate modulators of neuronal signalling that warrant further investigation in primary neurons and in vivo models.

title: Long-read nanopore sequencing of autism susceptibility genes: an exploratory study in adults with autism spectrum disorder.
abstract: This exploratory pilot study explores the feasibility of long-read nanopore whole-genome sequencing for the descriptive characterization of autism susceptibility genes in adults with late-diagnosed autism spectrum disorder (ASD) without intellectual disability or language impairment. This approach allows the simultaneous analysis of structural variants (SVs) and DNA methylation, including in repetitive and non-coding regions that are difficult to resolve with short-read methods. Nanopore whole-genome sequencing was performed on DNA from peripheral blood samples of 10 individuals with ASD and 10 sex- and age-matched non-autistic controls (NC). SVs and CpG island methylation of autism susceptibility genes listed in the Simons Foundation Autism Research Initiative (SFARI) Human Gene Database were compared descriptively between groups, with methylation analyzed in group-wise pooled data. SVs called in all ASD but in none of the NC samples were annotated and systematically compared with population reference datasets. Using exploratory thresholds, 27 CpG islands showed potential methylation differences (≥ 5%) between the pooled groups, the largest (32.5%, driven by 5-methylcytosine) in a CpG island in exon 2 of the HLA-DRB1 gene; smaller differences were found, among others, in DLGAP2, DPP6, GABRB3 and CACNA1A. None of the 269 SVs called in all ASD but in none of the NC samples was classified as pathogenic, 256 were located exclusively in introns, and 204 (75.8%) matched SVs catalogued in population reference data, mostly as common polymorphisms. In this small, descriptive pilot study, nanopore long-read sequencing enabled the simultaneous assessment of SVs and DNA methylation in autism susceptibility genes of adults with ASD without intellectual disability. No ASD-specific pathogenic SV was identified, and the methylation differences, derived from pooled data without independent validation or functional analyses, may partly reflect genetic or cell-type-related variation. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in larger cohorts. Not applicable.

title: Perimenopausal depression and risk of premature mortality: a register-based matched cohort study.
abstract: Depression during the perimenopausal age affects a large proportion of women, yet its potential role in long-term mortality risk, especially cause-specific mortality, remains poorly understood. We aimed to determine the long-term mortality risk following depression diagnosed during perimenopausal age. Matched cohort study using linked Swedish national and regional registers. We identified women born 1948-1977 and residing in Sweden during 2003-2022. Depression diagnoses during perimenopausal age (45-55 years) were identified from primary and specialist care. We matched these women with 10 unexposed women based on birth year and residence. All-cause and cause-specific mortality within a maximum of 20-year follow-up, expressed as hazard ratios adjusted for potential confounders (aHR). 113,868 women received a diagnosis of perimenopausal-age depression (referred as PMPD thereafter; mean age: 49.2, standard deviation: 2.9). The mortality rate (per 100,000 person-years) for women with PMPD was 469.5 versus 267.0 for unexposed women (n = 1,138,680). Compared to unexposed women, women with PMPD had an increased risk for all-cause mortality (aHR 1.21, 95% CI 1.18-1.25), particularly due to suicide (aHR 4.72, 95% CI 4.20-5.31) but also due to natural causes, for example, neurodegenerative diseases (aHR 1.46, 95% CI 1.20-1.77). Increased risk was also observed when restricting to women with menopausal and perimenopausal disorders and/or menopausal hormone therapy within ±4 years of PMPD diagnosis (aHR 1.14, 95% CI 1.08-1.21). The risk was stronger among women with PMPD with history of premenstrual disorders (aHR 1.57, 95% CI 1.17-2.10) or postpartum depression (aHR 2.06, 95% CI 1.30-3.26). An increased risk for mortality was also observed in sibling comparison (aHR 1.44, 95% CI 1.32-1.58).​ CONCLUSIONS: Women diagnosed with depression during perimenopausal age had an elevated risk of mortality, particularly due to suicide but also due to natural causes, with the highest risk occurring shortly after diagnosis. These findings highlight the need for timely and sustained mental health support among women during perimenopause.

title: The GUTS GO study: rationale and study design of a longitudinal high-risk youth cohort.
journal: Child and adolescent psychiatry and mental health
abstract: What factors contribute to the increased risk for antisocial behavior in youth, and more importantly, what explains why most youth at risk desist when they grow older? In the Growing Up Together in Society (GUTS) research program, we aim to answer these vital questions from a biopsychosocial perspective in a longitudinal cohort study. The GUTS GO cohort study specifically focuses on youth at risk who have difficulties in pursuing personal and societal goals. The main objective of this study is to explore why, even though some youth show early signs of antisocial behavior, most adolescents do not continue to display antisocial behavior. We will examine the social, contextual, biological, and behavioral mechanisms involved in the persistence or desistance of antisocial behavior, with main focus on the role of self-regulation, empathy and trust. We aim to assess the impact on adolescents' functioning in various societal contexts, including educational settings, social relationships, and adherence to societal norms. In this paper, we describe in detail the design of the GUTS GO study, the study population, the determinants, intermediate neurocognitive measures, and outcomes. Furthermore, we provide a detailed description of the procedures for inclusion, informed consent, recruitment, and our collaboration with network partners.Keywords: Adolescence; Antisocial Behavior; Youth at Risk; Self-regulation; Empathy; Trust; Longitudinal Cohort; Neurocognitive Development.

title: Atg7 deficiency in Tmem119-Cre-targeted cells causes sustained neuroimmune dysregulation and disrupts early postnatal brain development.
abstract: Autophagy is a critical regulator of immune homeostasis, but the role of autophagy-related gene 7 (Atg7) in microglia during early postnatal brain development remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated how Atg7 deficiency in Tmem119-Cre-targeted brain cells influences postnatal neuroimmune homeostasis and brain development. Conditional Atg7 knockout mice were generated by crossing Atg7flox/flox mice with Tmem119-Cre mice. Postnatal growth, survival, brain histology, ultrastructure, and transcriptomic changes in sorted microglia-enriched CD45+ cells were evaluated using molecular, histological, and ultrastructural analyses. Atg7 deficiency in Tmem119-Cre-targeted cells was associated with severe postnatal growth retardation, disproportionate brain retention, hair loss and shortened survival. In the brain, Atg7 deficiency was associated with progressive disruption of microglial homeostasis features, characterized by reduced microglial abundance, simplified morphology, and decreased expression of homeostatic markers. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed persistent inflammatory reprogramming enriched for type I interferon signaling, innate immune responses, and antigen processing and presentation pathways. These findings were supported by increased cortical expression of interferon-responsive genes and pro-inflammatory cytokines. These neuroimmune alterations were associated with astrogliosis, altered oligodendrocyte-lineage development, and dysregulated myelination, indicating impaired postnatal brain maturation. Our findings indicate that Atg7 deficiency in Tmem119-Cre-targeted brain cells is associated with disrupted neuroimmune homeostasis, accompanied by alterations in cortical development and myelination. These results support an important role for Atg7 in maintaining neuroimmune homeostasis during early postnatal brain maturation.

title: Knowledge translation and evidence use in medicinal cannabis policy: An evidence brief on regulation, effectiveness, safety and stakeholder support in Colombia.
abstract: In Colombia, formulating and implementing regulatory frameworks for safe access to medicinal cannabis (MC) is significantly challenging. The objective of this study is to mobilize available scientific evidence, public opinions and stakeholders' perspectives to support policy formulation regulating the use of medicinal cannabis. We conducted a knowledge translation process based on a strategy composed of four components: (1) identifying the best available scientific evidence regarding three elements previously defined in collaboration with decision-makers from Colombia's Ministry of Health and synthesizing it into an evidence brief, (2) organizing citizens panels (n = 20 citizens) to deliberate on the findings from the evidence brief, (3) developing a policy dialogue with key stakeholders (n = 32 stakeholders) from relevant organization to the issue and (4) conducting semistructured interviews with decision-makers (n = 4 decision-makers) to document their perceptions of the process and any policy developments they associated with it. Evidence was organized and deliberated across three policy elements: (1) regulation limits, where evidence shows that permissible tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) thresholds in MC products vary across jurisdictions, commonly ranging between 0.2 and 1%; (2) effectiveness and safety, where evidence supports MC use for chronic pain, adjunctive treatment for refractory epilepsy and alleviation of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting, with uncertainty persisting due to low- to moderate-quality evidence; and (3) training and communication, where educational strategies were shown to be effective at increasing clinical confidence, yet healthcare personnel perceived their current training as insufficient. Deliberation with citizens and stakeholders was conducted around these three elements. Participants identified the lack of clear and accessible information as the primary barrier to informed decision-making, emphasizing the need for professional training, evidence-based guidelines and monitoring mechanisms. Findings derived from evidence and citizen dialogues highlight key aspects informing public policies on MC. Despite regulatory advancements in cannabis, uncertainties remain regarding considerations for establishing regulatory limits and their potential consequences. The dearth of high-quality studies obfuscates the efficacy and safety of medicinal cannabis. Lastly, education of healthcare professionals and the community is imperative for the successful implementation of regulatory frameworks and informed decision-making.

title: Longitudinal associations of objectively measured sedentary behaviour and physical activity intensities with urinary incontinence among middle-aged women: a cohort study.
abstract: Urinary incontinence is a prevalent condition among middle-aged women, yet its relationship with activity behaviours remains underexplored. This study aimed to explore the longitudinal associations between objectively measured sedentary behaviour and physical activity intensities with urinary incontinence and its types in middle-aged Finnish women. A total of 224 women aged 47-55 years at baseline, drawn from the ERMA and EsmiRs studies were included. The prevalence of stress, urgency and mixed urinary incontinence symptoms was assessed using a structured questionnaire. Sedentary behaviour and physical activity were objectively measured using hip-worn accelerometers at baseline and at 4-year follow-up. Logistic generalized estimating equation models were used to analyse the associations between sedentary behaviour and different physical activity intensities with urinary incontinence, adjusting for potential confounders. Higher light-intensity physical activity was associated with slightly increased odds of urinary incontinence (OR = 1.004, 95% CI: 1.000 to 1.008, p = 0.043), specifically stress urinary incontinence (OR = 1.007, 95% CI: 1.002 to 1.0011, p = 0.002). Sedentary behaviour showed an inverse relationship with urinary incontinence and stress urinary incontinence that disappeared when accounting for all activity behaviours. No significant associations were observed for moderate or vigorous physical activity. No consistent harmful or beneficial associations of physical activity or sedentary behaviour with urinary incontinence were found in middle-aged women. The marginal link between light physical activity and stress urinary incontinence may reflect behavioural adaptations among symptomatic women. Future research should investigate how the type of physical behaviour, rather than its intensity, and long-term activity patterns, as opposed to short- or medium-term, may influence urinary incontinence in this population.

title: Long-read sequencing reveals RNA splicing dynamics in microglial aging and inflammation.
abstract: Microglia, the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, undergo age-associated transcriptional and functional remodeling implicated in multiple neurodegenerative diseases. Yet bulk and single-cell short-read RNA sequencing lack the resolution to full-length transcripts, leaving the isoform landscape of aging microglia and its alternative splicing regulation incompletely defined. Here, we present an isoform-centric landscape of microglial aging generated by Nanopore long-read RNA sequencing of purified microglia from male mice across 5 ages (2, 8, 12, 16, and 20 months), complemented by single-cell isoform sequencing to map isoform usage across homeostatic and reactive microglial subpopulations, and by acute lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge in young (2 months) and aged (20 months) mice. Across the aging trajectory, we cataloged 108,381 transcript isoforms from 25,439 genes, including 57,647 previously unannotated isoforms, revealing isoform-resolved aging programs and aging-related transcript usage switches that were frequently uncoupled from gene-level differential expression. Leveraging isoform RNA-seq at single-cell resolution, we mapped aging-associated isoforms to disease-associated microglia (DAM) and interferon-response microglia (IRM), providing a subtype-specific reference for interrogating isoform switching across microglial states. We further delineated how aging shapes LPS-evoked isoform response and identified microglial co-expression modules linked to neurodegenerative disease risk. Together, our study provides an isoform-resolved resource of microglial state diversification and age-dependent inflammatory responsiveness, and identifies isoform changes and splicing-associated modules that merit future mechanistic validation in neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.

title: Systemic and local oxidative stress biomarkers in periodontitis: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: To update and extend our previously published 2019 systematic review by evaluating oxidative stress (OS) biomarkers in saliva, gingival crevicular fluid (GCF), and blood in relation to periodontitis. We systematically searched five electronic databases including PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI) up to May 2025. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled to compare biomarker levels between periodontitis patients and healthy controls. A total of 62 studies were included. Notably, substantial between-study heterogeneity (most I2 > 50%) was detected across pooled analyses. Total antioxidant capacity (TAOC) was significantly reduced in periodontitis patients across all sample types (blood: SMD = -1.94; saliva: SMD = -1.01; GCF: SMD = -2.30). Malondialdehyde (MDA) was elevated in blood (SMD = 1.06), saliva (SMD = 1.63), and GCF (SMD = 2.50). 8-Hydroxy-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and nitric oxide (NO) were significantly elevated in saliva and GCF, and blood and saliva, respectively. Total oxidant status (TOS) was elevated in saliva and GCF but not in blood. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidase (GPx) did not show significant differences. Periodontitis is merely associated rather than causally linked with impaired antioxidant capacity and elevated oxidative stress, particularly in local biofluids. Although saliva and GCF show higher detection sensitivity than blood, such superiority needs further validated by well-designed comparative statistical studies.

title: Neurons, networks and causal equilibrium - toward a layered neuroontology for the neurosciences.
abstract: Contemporary neuroscience has made significant empirical advances, yet it often lacks a unified biological theoretical framework to integrate findings across cellular and systems levels. In this paper, we propose a layered neuroontology that distinguishes three foundational levels of brain organization: neurons, structural networks, and functional networks. Drawing on insights from neurophilosophy, systems neuroscience, and metaphysics, the framework emphasizes the ontological and epistemological distinctiveness of each level. Neurons are treated as discrete, mechanistically describable biological units; structural networks as physical, neuroanatomical connections; and functional networks as emergent, dynamic patterns of coordinated activity. We argue that functional networks are not reducible to their structural or neuronal substrates but represent higher-order organizational principles essential for understanding cognition and behavior. In addition, we propose a causal taxonomy describing how causal potential, causal restraint, and causal equilibrium are expressed across different levels of neural organization. This layered neuroontology has methodological, theoretical, and clinical implications, particularly in disorders where disruptions occur across multiple levels of brain organization. Applying a layered neuroontology to empirical practice yields a principled way to interpret data, design experiments, and target interventions.

title: Clinical characteristics and adrenaline use in anaphylaxis in children: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: This study aimed to analyze the clinical characteristics and adrenaline use in anaphylaxis in children, providing evidence to optimize the management strategies for anaphylaxis. A retrospective analysis was performed on 115 pediatric patients with anaphylaxis treated at Hangzhou Children's Hospital from January 2021 to October 2024. The analysis included age, gender, suspected triggers, allergy history, clinical manifestations, treatments, adverse reactions, and outcomes. Data on adverse reactions were collected from 70 children who received intramuscular adrenaline for non-anaphylaxis. Among the 115 patients, 37 had a prior history of allergy. The primary suspected triggers were food allergens (52/115, 45.22%) and drug allergens (34/115, 29.57%). Skin and mucosal involvement were the most common clinical manifestations, observed in 108 of 115 patients (93.91%), and typically presented as urticaria or angioedema. Respiratory symptoms were the second most frequent, occurring in 104 patients (90.43%), with manifestations including cough, wheezing, dyspnea, and laryngeal edema. Intramuscular adrenaline was administered to 101 patients (87.83%), with 91 patients (79.13%) receiving it as the first-line treatment. No adverse reaction was observed in either the anaphylaxis or non-anaphylaxis groups following adrenaline administration. No significant adverse reaction was reported in any of the children treated with adrenaline. Pediatric anaphylaxis faces a dual challenge of delayed adrenaline administration and excessive prophylactic use. Given the diagnostic difficulty of anaphylaxis in children, early administration of adrenaline, when anaphylaxis is strongly suspected clinically, may help optimize clinical management.

title: Retraction Note: Oncogenic Ras is downregulated by ARHI and induces autophagy by Ras/AKT/mTOR pathway in glioblastoma.
Smoking cessation information seeking in Türkiye following plain packaging, COVID-19, and the varenicline recall: a 10-year interrupted time series analysis.
abstract: Türkiye became the first country to fully implement all World Health Organization (WHO) MPOWER measures and introduced mandatory plain packaging for tobacco products in December 2019. Shortly thereafter, the COVID-19 pandemic and the global recall of varenicline disrupted smoking cessation efforts. We aimed to quantify the associations of these three sequential events with smoking cessation information-seeking behavior in Türkiye over a 10-year period. Weekly Relative Search Volume (RSV) data were extracted from Google Trends (Web Search and YouTube Search) for Türkiye between December 2015 and March 2026 (N = 536 weeks). Eight of 17 candidate Turkish search terms were retained after a prespecified validation step and grouped into four thematic clusters. A multiple interrupted time series (ITS) regression with Newey-West standard errors was used to estimate level and trend changes at each event, adjusting for seasonality. Effect sizes, Granger causality tests, an exploratory counterfactual projection, and extensive sensitivity analyses were performed. In the primary weekly model, plain packaging was associated with a positive but statistically non-significant immediate level change (β = 20.11; 95% CI - 3.47 to 43.69; p = 0.095). In pre-pandemic sensitivity analyses, post-policy search volume exceeded seasonally matched windows of the four preceding years (Cohen's d = 1.50; +61.8%; p < 0.001). An exploratory counterfactual projection estimated a 10,697-unit excess over the projected pre-policy trend (95% bootstrap interval 4,415-16,850). COVID-19 onset (β = -29.91; p = 0.002) and the varenicline recall (β = -11.91; p = 0.001) were associated with significant immediate declines; the recall was followed by a positive recovery trend (β = 0.165; p < 0.001). Pharmacological-cluster increases during the pandemic and after the recall were largely attributable to the dual-indication term "bupropion". Web searches Granger-predicted YouTube searches (p < 0.001, robust to differencing); the reverse was non-significant. Plain packaging implementation was followed by increased cessation-related search interest, although this association cannot be fully separated from the closely following COVID-19 period. Health crises and medication supply disruptions were associated with suppressed general cessation-related searching. Because search interest reflects information seeking rather than quit attempts, the implications for primary care are hypothesis-generating.

title: Adjunctive transcranial direct current stimulation in super-refractory status epilepticus: a prospective case series.
abstract: Super-refractory status epilepticus (SRSE) is a life-threatening neurological emergency characterized by persistent seizures despite anesthetic therapy, with high associated mortality and limited treatment options. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a potential neuromodulatory intervention in refractory epilepsy; however, evidence in SRSE remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and exploratory clinical response associated with adjunctive tDCS in patients with SRSE. In this investigator-initiated prospective single-center interventional case series, 20 adult patients with convulsive SRSE admitted to a tertiary referral center between 2021 and 2025 received adjunctive cathodal tDCS (2 mA for 20 min) applied bilaterally over temporal-frontal regions while standard medical therapy was continued. Clinical and electroencephalographic (EEG) assessments were performed 30 min before and after stimulation. Feasibility and safety were primary outcomes, while short-term clinical response was assessed as an exploratory endpoint. Written informed consent for study participation and publication of anonymized clinical data and EEG recordings was obtained from legally authorized representatives prior to enrollment, and the trial was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20230209057371N1; retrospectively registered on October 21, 2023). Four patients (20%; 95% CI: 6-44%) demonstrated short-term clinical and EEG improvement within 30 min of stimulation. No serious adverse events were observed; one patient experienced a mild, self-limited erythematous skin reaction. Hospital mortality was 50%. Exploratory subgroup differences were observed between responders and non-responders. Adjunctive tDCS was feasible and well tolerated in patients with SRSE, with short-term clinical and EEG improvement observed in a subset of patients. These preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in controlled, adequately powered studies to determine efficacy and identify predictors of response. This study was registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT) under registration number IRCT20230209057371N1 on October 21, 2023. The trial was registered while participant recruitment was ongoing (retrospective registration relative to study initiation).

title: "I didn't even know humans could get polio … I swear that's for dogs." A co-produced, thematic analysis exploring adolescent attitudes to vaccines.
abstract: Immunisation forms a cornerstone of public health policy. However, uptake rates of routine vaccines offered in adolescence are sub-optimal. In 2023/24, for example, HPV uptake in England, for example, was 72.9% of girls and 67.7% of boys in school year 8 (aged 12 to 13 years), well below the World Health Organization's goal of achieving 90% coverage by 2030. This presents both individual and public health risks. While much research exists on the attitudes of healthcare workers and parents towards adolescent vaccines, less is heard from adolescents themselves. We worked with over 80 adolescents to co-design, pilot and analyse data for this qualitative thematic analysis of adolescent attitudes towards vaccines. Adolescent collaborators received training in qualitative research methods and thematic analysis and contributed to study design by selecting the interview format, co-developing participant materials and the discussion guide, leading piloting activities with younger adolescents, and contributing to coding, theme development and interpretation of findings. For the study itself, we interviewed 30 adolescents aged 12-17 years living in England. Participants were generally in favour of some or all vaccines, with a minority having not received any adolescent vaccines. Five themes were identified: Understanding vaccines, Fear and comfort; Autonomy and control; Information sources and conspiracy theories; and Identity and social norms. Among our participants, vaccine uptake was influenced by perceptions of vaccine preventable diseases and by fear of needles. Decision-making dynamics between parents and adolescents were complex, with autonomy disrupting as well as driving vaccine behaviour. Social media was not a major source of vaccine information for adolescents, with participants expressing disinterest in online vaccine content and implicating adults as the ones engaging with and sharing online vaccine disinformation. Finally, we found that adolescent development impacted vaccine attitudes. Younger participants were more likely to adopt a collective family attitude toward vaccines. Older participants were more able to consider long-term benefits and more likely to have established their own position on vaccines. In our study, most participants wanted to be more involved in vaccine decisions; given techniques to manage anxiety about vaccines; better educated about vaccine preventable diseases; and supported in developing the critical thinking skills needed to make informed health decisions.

title: Intranasal dexmedetomidine versus intravenous propofol for the prevention of pediatric emergence delirium following general anesthesia: A randomized controlled trial.
